headline: Micron has opened a second plant in Taichung, Taiwan, that packages and tests the AI memory chips known as HBM, while a profit-sharing dispute with its Taiwanese union is still open.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 to 5: the opening took place on 15 Oct and our 15 Oct edition already carried it and the union dispute; this adds capacity, Singapore and rally details.
importance_line: It affects Micron's workers in Taiwan, who won a vote for the right to strike over a demand for 15 percent of operating profit, and buyers of AI memory, though what is announced so far is a rally on 19 Oct and a deadline of 22 Oct for further action.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports, citing Taiwan's Economic Daily News and Commercial Times, that Micron, the world's third-largest memory chipmaker, held the opening ceremony on 15 Oct 2026 for its second advanced assembly and test plant in Taichung, where Donghui Lu, chairman of Micron Taiwan, said orders for its high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked memory paired with AI processors, are fully booked through 2027 and a further HBM packaging plant will open in Singapore in 2027. Our 15 Oct 2026 edition carried The Edge Malaysia's report that Taiwan's president urged Micron and its union to negotiate at this opening; new today are the capacity and Singapore details and the union's plan for a rally near the Presidential Office on 19 Oct, with further action if there is no deal by 22 Oct.
notes: Full text read (AI-translated from Korean). Follows item 46 of our 15 Oct 2026 edition (The Edge Malaysia, Taiwan's president at the Micron opening). Not marked follow-up in the chunk; treated as one because the event is 15 Oct.
